root_refinement: Make positive kappa/sound speed/healing length and zero-damping edge explicit, as identified by independent review.
before_paragraph:
The condensate rows share a structure. Both corrections scale as
$\kappa^2$ at fixed platform, $\delta_{\rm disp}$ through
$D = \kappa\xi/c_s$ and $\delta_{\rm diss}$ through
$\Gamma_H \propto (\kappa/c_s)^2$, so their ratio is independent of
$\kappa$ within a given configuration and varies by orders of magnitude
between configurations. This makes the ratio, not either correction
separately, the quantity a single apparatus can vary and measure. A
scattering-length sweep changes $\xi$ and $c_s$ at fixed geometry and
moves the ratio without moving $\kappa$, which is the cleanest available
handle on the dissipative sector.
after_paragraph:
The condensate rows compare corrections with different dependence on
surface gravity. At fixed healing length, sound speed and first-order
transport coefficients, Eqs.~\eqref{eq:delta-disp} and~\eqref{eq:delta-diss}
give $\delta_{\rm disp} \propto -\kappa^2$ and
$\delta_{\rm diss} \propto \kappa$, respectively. For $\kappa>0$, $c_s>0$ and $\xi>0$, their ratio is therefore
\begin{equation}
\frac{\delta_{\rm diss}}{|\delta_{\rm disp}|}
  = \frac{6(\gamma_1+\gamma_2)}{\pi\xi^2\kappa},
\end{equation}
For positive damping this decreases inversely with $\kappa$ under those
fixed-material conditions; at zero damping the ratio vanishes. The zero-temperature Beliaev matching used for the benchmark
rows has the same dependence: $\Gamma_H \propto \kappa^2$ at fixed
upstream density, scattering length and sound speed, and the correction
is $\Gamma_H/\kappa$, not $\Gamma_H$ itself. The ratio distinguishes the
benchmark configurations, but is not invariant under a surface-gravity
sweep. A scattering-length sweep changes the healing length, sound speed
and microscopic damping together; its effect on the ratio must be
computed with the background and surface gravity recomputed, rather than
assuming that fixed geometry holds $\kappa$ fixed. These are scaling
statements within the adopted transport and background models, not a
microscopic derivation of those models.
scientific_scope: Fixed-material algebra within existing adopted models, no microscopic BUILD discharge
